title: Merge Two Linked Lists Alternately
description:
Given the heads of two singly linked lists `l1` and `l2`, merge them into a single linked list by alternating nodes starting with `l1`: `l1[0], l2[0], l1[1], l2[1], ...`.

If one list is longer than the other, append all remaining nodes of the longer list to the end of the merged list. Return the head of the merged list in `O(n + m)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in each list is in the range [0, 5000].
hints: Maintain a sentinel `dummy` and `tail` pointer; in each iteration while both `l1` and `l2` are non-null, save `l1.next` and `l2.next`, append `l1` then `l2` to `tail`, and advance both lists.
After the loop finishes, attach whichever of `l1` or `l2` is still non-null directly to `tail.next`.

examples.explanation: Taking nodes alternately from [1, 3, 5] and [2, 4, 6] gives [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6].
After alternating 1, 10, 2, 20, the remaining nodes [30, 40] of l2 are appended.
When l1 is empty, all nodes of l2 are returned as-is.
